By decreasing the initial catalyst concentration to 0.05, we can strongly test M3: because M3 relies on a catalyst dimer, its active site concentration scales with [cat]^2, meaning the rate will drop significantly more than for monomeric catalyst models.
Additionally, by introducing an initial product concentration of 0.2, we can simultaneously test for product-induced deactivation (M12, M17) or product inhibition. If these mechanisms are active, the reaction will show an immediately reduced initial rate or early plateau compared to models without product sensitivity.
This combination of lower S, lower cat, and added P will effectively separate the top models by probing their distinct non-linear dependencies.
